text:
oncall-bot: PAGER — Sev 2 — multi-GPU collective instability observed in tp4-prod (nccl hangs/timeouts). Affected pool: tp4-gpu. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nccl-collective|nccl-collective>. Escalation: eng-sre, infra.

maya: spotted repeated communicator timeouts on gpuhost-12. pods restarting. posting logs.

raj: i'm oncall; joining. paste the latest nccl/cuda block pls.

maya: logs pasted below.
```
2026-03-15T15:40:12.001Z ERROR nccl: ReduceScatter timed out after 110s, rank 1->2 stalled
2026-03-15T15:40:13.345Z ERROR cuda: driver Xid 79 (GPU page fault) pid=8754 /usr/bin/runtime
2026-03-15T15:40:13.346Z INFO containerd: oom_kill: pid=8754 oom_score_adj=0 name=redwood-runtime
2026-03-15T15:40:13.678Z WARN k8s: pod tp4-train-12 CrashLoopBackOff restarts=4
```

sam: context — we launched a pipeline-parallel job across 4 GPUs at ~15:30, micro-batch 32, seq 6144. looks like heavy KV allocation + collectives.

luis: node metrics: gpuhost-12 GPU mem at 99% across cards; thermal spike recorded at 15:38 on GPU#2.

infra-bot: k8s events recent:
```
NAMESPACE   NAME                   READY STATUS            RESTARTS AGE
tp4         tp4-train-12-abc        0/1   CrashLoopBackOff    4      25m
node        gpuhost-12             N/A   NotReady            3m
```

raj: immediate customer impact check — amy-cs?

amy-cs: two enterprise customers reported failed training jobs (error: "worker hung"). 5 self-serve jobs also hit. Marking P0 for impacted enterprise customers: gamma-ai and delta-analytics.

ops-bot: routing health — requests for tp4 routes are still landing in tp4-gpu pool. Auto-fallback disabled for XID patterns currently.

raj: mitigation steps (short): 1) isolate gpuhost-12 (cordon) 2) trigger fallback routing for impacted customers -> tp4-solo 3) collect core dumps and dmesg 4) restart driver on node if safe 5) schedule hardware quarantine if driver reset fails.

maya: cordon executed: `kubectl cordon gpuhost-12` -> Success. Starting drain with `--ignore-daemonsets`

maya: drain triggered, but noticed node flapped NotReady during drain. some pods evicted, training job in CrashLoop.

luis: ssh to node, grabbing dmesg and nvml logs. dmesg shows: repeated Xid 79 and a GPU reset:
```
[ 54321.987654] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, PID=8754, GPU page fault during activity, reason: GPU memory access error.
[ 54321.987800] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00:00: Xid 79, GPU RESET
```

sam: hypothesis — driver-level page fault causing cuda process termination -> nccl/allreduce hang because one rank disappears. Could be model memory access pattern triggering driver bug.

raj: workaround route — sam can you trigger fallback for gamma-ai and delta-analytics via control plane? command: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/routing/force-fallback -d '{"pool":"tp4-gpu","target":"tp4-solo","filter":"customer:gamma-ai|delta-analytics"}'`

sam: executing now. API returned 200. ops-bot shows 3 active sessions re-routed. Jobs will run slower but continue.

maya: attempted `systemctl restart nvidia-driver` on gpuhost-12 -> driver restarted but CRITICAL: runtime container for tp4-train-12 still OOM'ing immediately. pod logs show same Xid 79 after ~30s.

luis: checked hardware: ECC error counts rising on GPU#2 and GPU#3. sending telemetry to infra.

infra-bot: created INFRA-4928: Quarantine gpuhost-12 and schedule replacement.

raj: handoff — sam, take lead for 45m. Tasks: collect /var/log/dmesg, nvml logs, container core dumps; reproduce in staging with same driver (525.85.05) and memory parameters; open vendor bug if reproducible.

sam: ack. saving artifacts to /incidents/3432199999/artifacts. creating ticket RDW-INC-2026-042.

maya: quick customer update posted: "We've routed your jobs to a single-GPU fallback and are investigating hardware-level GPU faults. ETA initial remediation 60m."

amy-cs: noted. customers notified.

sam: reproduction attempt on staging with driver 525.85.05 and identical workload reproduces reduced allreduce failure after ~100s. capturing strace and nvprof. filing to vendor with logs and core dumps.

luis: suggestion — add detection for Xid 79 in our observability pipeline to trigger immediate fallback. right now Xid events only surface as logs.

raj: agreed. adding short-term runbook change: treat Xid 79 as immediate fallback trigger; reduce worker retry/exponential backoff to avoid rescheduling on same node.

ops-bot: created alert rule alerts/auto-fallback-on-xid79 and temporarily enabled at 0.3 sensitivity.

sam: mitigation summary: - quarantined node gpuhost-12 - rerouted impacted customer sessions to tp4-solo - collected artifacts and reproduced issue in staging - vendor bug filed RDW-VND-2026-115 - created INFRA ticket for hardware replacement - runbook updated to auto-fallback on Xid79

maya: impact note: ~6% throughput reduction in tp4 pool while quarantines/repairs in progress; 7 jobs failed and were retried via fallback.

amy-cs: customer comms: told gamma-ai/delta-analytics about fallback and ETA 90m for HW replacement scheduling.

raj: leaving a post-handoff note — i'll follow up in 2 hours for RCA and confirm vendor response. thanks team.

sam: monitoring for 45m, will escalate to hardware replacement if driver reset does not prevent Xid 79 within that window.

maya: adding temporary dashboard rule: if >2 Xid79 events on a single node within 15m -> cordon and auto-fallback. ops-bot enabled the rule.

ops-bot: rule created: alerts/cordon-on-xid79.

infra-bot: node gpuhost-12 set to quarantine, autoscaler blacklisted.

maya: closing thread. reopen if customer impact widens. :white_check_mark:"
